body: The Wells Fargo Tower at 90 S. Cascade Ave. and the FirstBank Building at 2 N. Cascade Ave., the two tallest buildings in Colorado Springs and part of the downtown Palmer Center, have fallen into foreclosure, The Gazette reported on August 25, 2026, citing El Paso County Public Trustee's Office records. A foreclosure notice was filed against RPalmer LLC, Overland Palmer LLC and Palmer Center Owner LLC, Delaware companies controlled by real estate firms with principal offices in California and Canada. A fourth entity, DPalmer LLC, was also noticed; it withdrew its authority to do business in Colorado in January 2021. Several business-suite properties reached through either building or the adjacent Antlers hotel are also in foreclosure, though The Gazette updated its story to clarify that the Antlers itself is not.

The owner entities bought the buildings in 2015, according to the county assessor. Records show an unpaid principal balance of about $59 million on a $74 million loan, which a trustee for Bank of America now holds, and a foreclosure auction was scheduled for October 21. The Gazette said it was unclear what caused the default and that it could not reach the attorney listed on the filing. The paper reported that tenants could likely keep operating as before.

The Gazette cited a Downtown Partnership report putting downtown office vacancy at 10.4% in the second quarter of 2026, against 12% citywide, with downtown Class A vacancy rising to 8.2% from 7.4%. A longtime Colorado Springs developer who is a FirstBank Building tenant called the foreclosures "a function of market circumstances."

timeline.label: The owner entities buy the Palmer Center buildings
Foreclosure notice filed with the El Paso County Public Trustee; The Gazette reports it August 25
Scheduled date for the foreclosure auction
